observed_defect: The non-terminal intermediate Qwen discriminator derives an affirmation/negative contrastive vector but its calibration and holdout propositions all map the desired response to literal YES and select on raw YES-minus-NO. A generic literal-YES bias can therefore satisfy the directional test without demonstrating proposition-dependent semantic control. The current promotion gate independently requires counterbalanced token-label mapping for scientific goal credit, so the existing executor cannot close that goal gate as written.
counterhypothesis: The intermediate intervention may still establish low-level mechanism evidence: an exact runtime may consume a non-terminal residual vector and show directional effects versus sign/null/orthogonal/permuted controls. The defect concerns semantic/scientific promotion, not whether vector bytes are consumed.
delta: Add a successor wrapper that preserves the exact base Qwen checkpoint/runtime/vector machinery.
Counterbalance calibration and holdout over true/false propositions and NORMAL/REVERSED YES/NO output mappings.
Select and adjudicate on expected-label-oriented margin rather than raw YES-minus-NO.
Require every calibration and holdout case to improve under +VECTOR and worsen under SIGN_FLIP, with null and same-norm nuisance controls retained.
Bind truthful vector-derivation metadata, output-token metric identity, counterbalanced-label declaration, source tree, clean worktree state, base-executor hash and wrapper hash.
Fail closed before runtime on a dirty source tree and discard a promotion candidate if source/head/tree/executor bytes drift during execution.
next_exact_action: Run the counterbalanced successor on an exact clean zero-cost Qwen3-0.6B source snapshot. A literal YES preference must fail paired reversed mappings. Only a mapping-invariant expected-label effect surviving sign/null/orthogonal/permuted controls may become a promotion candidate, then it must pass the separate current promotion gate and source-bound promotion boundary before any model-specific scientific credit is considered.
